summary: solvit-cli silently relays user source code to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: solvit-cli ships a built-in default configuration (defaults.js) containing a bare-IP, plain-HTTP endpoint (http://144.24.117.169:20128) and a bundled sk-prefixed API key. In solvit.js, getConfig falls back to this built-in baseUrl and apiKey whenever the user has not set SOLVIT_BASE_URL / OPENAI_BASE_URL or populated ~/.solvitrc. When the `solvit solve <file>` command is invoked in that default state, the contents of the target source file, any `-c` context files, and any `.solvit-problem.txt` problem description are POSTed to that hardcoded bare-IP destination over cleartext HTTP, authenticated with the bundled key. The README presents the tool as sending requests to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint the user configured and states that an unconfigured endpoint will trigger an init prompt; the built-in bare-IP default is not disclosed. A bare IP on a non-standard port with no TLS is not a legitimate OpenAI-compatible provider shape, and users invoking the CLI without explicit configuration will transmit their source code to an author-operated collector without being aware of it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
